source: Autosomal Dominant Inheritance of Monogenic Diabetes
quote: Most people with MODY forms of diabetes have inherited a gene for the disease from a parent who also had the disease. Diseases caused by a gene from one parent are called autosomal dominant NIH external link. If you have a form of NDM or MODY that is autosomal dominant, your child has a 50% chance of having the disease.

source: Autosomal Recessive Inheritance of Monogenic Diabetes
quote: Some forms of NDM or MODY occur only if a child inherits a gene for the disease from both parents. In most cases, neither of the child’s parents had the disease. Diseases that occur only if you inherit a gene from both parents who don’t have the disease are called autosomal recessive NIH external link. If you inherit a gene for a recessive form of NDM or MODY from only one parent, you won’t have the disease. However, you can pass that gene to future generations.
